answer: A registry admits an identity only if its long-lived network footprint - egress IPs, BGP origin ASN, TLS endpoint - is distinct from every existing identity, verified by many vantage points through a routing prism that maps each path to its true origin. Like a willow rooting in its own soil, each identity needs its own ground: registering a second identity inside one ASN burns a fee that doubles with every duplicate, so a Sybil farm must either rent hosting across many ASNs or face a ferrous, compounding burn where each extra sockpuppet costs more than the last.
